statement: Comparison for U005: 'retrieval-agnostic' should not be presented as a contribution. Retriever-agnostic temporal filtering already exists in another form - an ontology-driven pre-retrieval filter that admits legal sources by jurisdiction, lifecycle status and temporal validity before retrieval - and temporal handling is elsewhere embedded across representation, retrieval and reasoning layers. At the same time, evidence from a regulatory QA benchmark shows base-retriever behaviour is not uniform (BM25 beats hybrid on multihop queries while hybrid wins overall), so portability cannot be assumed and must be measured. The honest status of the plug-in framing is therefore a design constraint plus an empirical result (per-retriever effect sizes and their consistency), not a claimed property of the mechanism; the difference from the ontology-governed filter is only that the proposed gate scores rather than hard-admits, which is an implementation detail.

evidence.quote: BM25 outperforms hybrid on multihop queries
the ontology filters legal sources by jurisdiction, topic, lifecycle status, and temporal validity
embeds temporal validity directly into the representation, retrieval, and reasoning layers of RAG systems
